input.quote: The construction and validity of this Agreement and the provisions hereof, and the rights and obligations of the Parties hereunder, will be governed by the internal laws of the State of Delaware, USA
input.rationale: Section 15.9 selects Delaware law, which sits squarely at the playbook fallback (Delaware law is an accepted jurisdiction), rather than the preferred New York law. On forum, Section 15.10 sends unresolved Disputes to ICDR arbitration, but the seat is expressly New York, the proceeding is governed by the U.S. Federal Arbitration Act, IP ownership/validity disputes are carved out for a U.S. federal court, and either Party may seek preliminary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction. That is not "mandatory arbitration seated abroad" nor a foreign venue in SFJ's home jurisdiction, so the walk-away trigger is not met and the material terms (accepted governing law, U.S./New York-seated forum) are satisfied. Noted but not flagged: the forum is arbitration rather than New York County courts, and Section 15.10.2.4 limits the arbitrators' authority to award consequential/punitive damages (a mutual waiver addressed under the liability rules, not here).
